correctness.rationale: The shift inverse is an exact polynomial identity on every odd cycle. Two-edge atoms yield nodal derivatives in {-2,0,2}; each quadratic cell contributes at most one to variation. Every zero-sum cyclic difference admits nonnegative transport decomposition with mass Vd/2, proving the all-data upper bound. A one-site spike attains n/2. For even n, the alternating null vector gives precisely the stated compatibility and nonuniqueness. Exact rational checker verifies 11,900 atom cases, 1,800 other inputs and even-cycle examples; the infinite claim rests on the analytic argument.

originality.rationale: The verified claim is the sharp n/2 variation coefficient for exact C1 quadratic knot interpolation on every odd finite cycle. General spline solvability and parity obstructions are known background, not separately claimed novel. Full-text Schoenberg 1968 and open-access Nochetto–Salgado 2012 involve different spline degrees and interpolation operators. The nearest published search records concern norms of linear orthogonal projectors. Goodman 1983 and Albasiny–Hoskins 1973 are material incomplete inspections, acknowledged as priority risks; no confirmed equivalent or stronger applicable theorem found.

value.rationale: The all-odd-n sharp n/2 amplification quantifies a natural exact-knot quadratic interpolation instability over infinitely many grid sizes. A one-site spike realizes every norm, while the even-n loss of unisolvence explains the parity mechanism. This is a complete stability classification, not a fixed finite census or simple unmotivated change of parameters, and it contrasts with variation-diminishing averaged interpolation.
